one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban addresses President Duterte's indignant martial-law threat against communist rebels during the COVID-19 emergency by anchoring the discussion in his own court's masterwork -- David v. Arroyo (May 3, 2006, penned by Justice Sandoval-Gutierrez). He concedes that the President's call-out power is facially constitutional under Art. VII, Sec. 18, but warns that 'as applied' implementation can be declared unconstitutional: David struck down the warrantless arrests of columnist Randy David and Ronald Llamas and the warrantless search of the Daily Tribune, reiterating the two valid bases for warrantless arrest (in flagrante and 'just been committed' with probable cause from personal knowledge). He extends the same logic to the Pacific Plaza Towers armed intrusion in Taguig and to the Cpl. Winston Ragos killing. He then takes a memoir-mode detour, listing the four most noteworthy Panganiban-Court decisions: David v. Arroyo; Senate v. Ermita (Carpio Morales, April 20, 2006, compelling Cabinet attendance at congressional inquiries); Bayan v. Ermita (Azcuna, April 25, 2006, throwing out 'Calibrated Preemptive Response'); and Lambino v. Comelec (Carpio, Oct 25, 2006, striking down the people's-initiative form-of-government change). He notes that Justices Gutierrez and Azcuna prefaced their ponencias with odes to his philosophy of liberty and prosperity and cited those decisions at their retirement as their obra maestra, while Justice Carpio's 'scathing' Lambino language ('deception', 'gigantic fraud on the people') is believed to have cost him the chief justiceship under his former client, Arroyo. He closes by quoting the Salonga-Miranda-Feliciano book 'A Test of Courage' (2007, 231-page Regina Publishing hardcover) -- 'The nation applauded the grit, sharpness and courage of the Panganiban Court... authoritarianism, "creeping" or blatant, has no place in our society' -- and notes that this 231-page tribute felt to him 'equal to, if not better than, the several honorary doctoral degrees' he had received. A short erratum corrects 'Neda Board' to 'PSA Board' in the prior Sunday's column.
